findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() throws NoSuchElementException when user storage does not expose CredentialModel
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns an `Optional<CredentialModel>` by streaming `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`. However, custom `UserStorageProvider` implementations that implement `CredentialInputValidator` and `CredentialInputUpdater` (such as the 4.8.3 backwards-compatibility storage, before this PR added `getCredentials` to it) are not required to override `getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)` (whose default implementation in `CredentialInputValidator` returns `Stream.empty()`). For such providers, `isConfiguredFor` returns `true`, so `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` challenges the user and renders the login form, instantiating `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`. Calling `credentialModelOpt.get()` (and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` on line 21) without checking `isPresent()` will throw `NoSuchElementException` when rendering the login form if the provider does not return a `CredentialModel` from `getCredentials()`.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException in getCredentials when user is not found in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage
findings.body: In `getCredentials(RealmModel realm, UserModel user)`, `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` can return `null` if the user is not present in the `users` map (note that `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, and `isValid` in the same class all guard against `myUser == null`). Dereferencing `myUser.recoveryCodes` on line 235 without a null check will throw a `NullPointerException` when `getCredentials` is invoked for a user not managed by this storage.
